# The docking system gets its Body-side architecture guide

## Context

Operator direction (2026-08-21/22, in-session): peers stopped understanding the architecture; the remedy that worked for the embedding lane — visualize the architecture so understanding enables action — becomes the house pattern: *"more guides about architecture. dock layout included."* Gated behind the harness-misnomer retirement: *"no guides as long as ADRs include harness"* — that condition CLEARED when PR #17507 merged (2026-08-21T22:04Z, `0e072f05cd`).

DockLayouts is the v13.2 centerpiece with many eyes on it. The docking substrate has deep authority documents — `learn/agentos/decisions/0029-docking-design.md` (prescriptive, ~560 lines) and `learn/agentos/DockZoneModel.md` (descriptive contract) — but NO conceptual guide: nothing a peer or an adopting app builder reads first to hold the whole system. The ADR's own history proves the gap: its §5 leaf table went 8+ cells stale without anyone noticing (`#17503`), and this session's `#16357` closed as already-resolved because nobody could see that a committed witness already guarded the class.

## The Problem

The docking system is the strongest Body capability with the weakest narrative surface. What exists is decision-tier and contract-tier; what's missing is the explanation tier (Diátaxis): who owns what (model / adapter / reconciler / zones / vessels / coordinator / arbiter), how ONE gesture actually runs through the seams, which state lives where (the §2.1 four-row table, told as a story), what an app must do to adopt docking (the workstation as the worked example), the wire vocabulary (8 shipped identifiers, two compatibility classes per §2.9), and the traps (layout-blind panes, no parallel drag system, the schema freeze, engine-paint tokens once `#17241` lands). Also missing: the honest moat story — the ADR §4 prior-art sweep shows no surveyed web library offers window-independent live-state docking; that story exists only inside a decision record nobody reads first.

## The Architectural Reality

- Home: `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts.md` — Body-side, sibling to `Layouts.md`. The dock is a Body capability; its conceptual guide belongs in the Body's learning tree (also extraction-proof: wave-one custody keeps learn trees Engine-owned, but a Body guide in the Body section is correct in every topology). The agentos-side ADR + contract stay the deep tier, linked.
- Registration inputs: `learn/tree.json` (`guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts`) + `buildScripts/docs/seo/generate.mjs` `PRIORITIES` (0.8, matching `Layouts`). ⛔ Generated `sitemap.xml`/`llms.txt` untouched (pipeline-owned).
- Grounding already banked this session (guide-authoring §1): the same-gesture witness run headed 4/4 green (the subsystem exercised through its own oracle), the full ADR + contract read end-to-end, the wire census derived from source, the `#16357` closure receipts, and lived material from the workstation film arc (including the `#17241` layer lesson learned the hard way).

## The Fix

Author the guide to the guide-authoring 9/10 bar: narrative arc (the enterprise desktop-to-web friction → why web docking fails at the popout boundary → the SharedWorker answer → what the reader's app gets), ≥1 render-verified `flowchart TD` (the ownership map; the one-gesture walkthrough), the state-class story, the adoption recipe, the wire vocabulary with its two compatibility classes, the traps, attributed lived voice, and links down to ADR 0029 + DockZoneModel.md for depth. No client names. Never "framework".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts.md` exists and clears the guide-authoring bar §§1–5 (grounding evidence in the PR body; self-grade against the bar included).
- [ ] ≥1 Mermaid `flowchart TD` render-verified in a browser before merge (method named in the PR).
- [ ] Registered in `learn/tree.json` (`ai:lint-tree-json` green) + the SEO `PRIORITIES` map; generated outputs untouched.
- [ ] Every factual claim V-B-A'd against current source/ADR states (post-#17503 names only); the wire vocabulary matches the §2.9 two-class table.
- [ ] Conceptual/reference split honored: no inlined tool catalogs or payload specs — those link to the contract doc.

## Out of Scope

- Rewriting ADR 0029 or `DockZoneModel.md` (deep tier stays as-is).
- The dockdemo relocation (`#16322`), styling promotion (`#17241`), examples normalization (`#17504`) — the guide cites their current truth and will be touched up by whoever lands them if paths move.
- A dock API reference page (generated-reference territory).

* fix(dashboard): the engine rail tab outranks the theme button floor (#17522)

Promoting the rail-tab paint engine-side deleted two working escape hatches.
Both apps carried their own higher-specificity `min-width: 0` because the engine
rule at (0,3,0) TIES `:root .neo-theme-* .neo-button` (also (0,3,0)), which
floors every button at 48px. Workstation's comment named the tie, the mechanism
and the symptom — "renders as an empty pill" — and I deleted the rule it was
attached to while writing prose claiming the tie was gone.

A leading `:root` lifts the engine rule to (0,4,0) so it outranks the theme
outright, and no consumer needs a local escape hatch for a working rail. The
stale prose in all three files is corrected, including an inherited comment that
miscounted the theme selector as (0,2,0).

`dockRailTabLayering.spec.mjs` gains a compiled-cascade oracle: it compiles
every stylesheet mentioning a button in-process (CI never runs build-themes, so
reading dist/ would match nothing and report green), finds each rule that can
reach a rail tab, and fails when any non-engine rule ties or beats the engine on
an engine-owned property. Source text cannot see this; the previous source-only
guard passed the defect.

Four mutations, each reddening its own arm: dropping the `:root` (the defect
itself), an app re-declaring min-width, the engine dropping the hover-background
token, and a top-level `:root` token leaking out of an app file. The first
attempt at that last mutation stayed green because a nested `:root` still
compiles under the app class — the arm was fine, the mutation was not.

Still open from the review: the close target's AC-3 and AC-6 need computed
styles in a live document. Next commit.

Reported-by: @neo-gpt-emmy
Co-Authored-By: Emmy <neo-gpt-emmy@neomjs.com>

* test(dashboard): a rendered rail tab witnesses the min-width release (#17522)

The close target's AC-3 and AC-6 ask for computed styles, which a compiled
selector comparison cannot supply. `DockRailTabPaint.spec.mjs` mounts a real
`Neo.dashboard.Container` with a real `DockRail` and measures the tab a browser
actually paints.

Three findings shaped the fixture, each caught by a control rather than by
inspection:

1. `empty-viewport` inherits DefaultConfig.themes, which carries the LEGACY
   themes plus one neo theme. The 48px `.neo-button` floor exists only in the
   neo pair, so a witness running there measures a document where the competing
   rule was never loaded. The new `dock-rail` fixture app pins both neo themes.
2. Mounting a plain container wearing `.neo-dashboard` leaves
   `src/dashboard/Container.css` unloaded — Neo loads a class's stylesheet when
   the class is instantiated — so the rule under test was absent and the arms
   measured the generic button skin. The fixture now mounts the real class.
3. The engine rule TRANSITIONS `color`. Reading straight after a class flip
   returns the start value and a frame later returns a blend (measured at
   rgb(244,172,171) en route to red). Transitions are switched off for the
   measurement; a sleep would only have made the flake slower.

Every min-width arm measures a plain sibling button FIRST and requires it to be
at the 48px floor. `min-width: 0px` on a rail tab only means the engine won if
the floor was live in the same document; without that control a theme that
simply failed to load reads as a pass — which is exactly what finding 1 was.

Mutation: dropping the `:root` from the engine rule reds both theme arms with
`Received: "48px"` — the empty-pill regression itself, on a rendered tab.

Component suite 53 passed; unit buildScripts + core 171 passed.

Reported-by: @neo-gpt-emmy
Co-Authored-By: Emmy <neo-gpt-emmy@neomjs.com>

* test(dashboard): the rail tab's paint is witnessed on both real consumers (#17522)

Discharges @neo-gpt-emmy's RA-2 remainder. Her disposition was exact: the
compiled-selector and source-guard clauses were addressed, but the runtime file
checked only `min-width` across themes and then injected a synthetic
`.test-app-a` rule. A rule authored in a spec is a rule nobody ships, so it
proved the engine's token plumbing and nothing about either app.

Five arms now load the COMPILED artifacts instead — the app's own stylesheet
plus the theme-scoped token layer its values reference, both from `dist/**`,
the same files Neo loads at runtime. Four measure background, color, border,
box-shadow and font-family resting and hovered, per app per neo theme. The
fifth puts both real consumers in one document and mutates one app's token.

Parity is asserted per state against the app's OWN palette token —
`--workstation-ink-dim` / `--workstation-ink`, `--fm-ink-dim` / `--fm-ink` —
which is what these tabs computed before the promotion, when the app declared
`color` directly. Border and box-shadow are asserted to stay engine-neutral in
both states: an app that re-declared either would be back in the
equal-specificity tie this promotion dissolved.

Three things this caught, each of which had been green or red for the wrong
reason:

The first version asserted `resting.color !== hovered.color` and called it "the
app's ink reaches the tab". Deleting the engine's resting `color:
var(--dock-rail-tab-color)` left all four arms GREEN — the separate hover rule
still moved the value, so two states differing proved neither came from where
the arm claimed. Against the tightened arms that same mutation reds all four
with `Expected: "rgb(139, 151, 168)" / Received: "rgb(0, 0, 0)"`.

The two-consumer arm first asserted the apps start with different ink. They do
not: workstation and FM share `#8b97a8` for dim ink in the dark theme, so the
precondition asserted a difference the design does not have. It is anchored on
voice instead — only workstation sets `--dock-rail-tab-font-family` — which is
where they genuinely diverge, and the asymmetry is asserted rather than
normalised away.

Loading an app's rule without its theme-scoped token layer leaves every `var()`
an invalid substitution, and the tab then computes the engine default under the
app's name. Both layers load, and a failed link rejects loudly rather than
skipping.
